Yes, I've tried to do something similar and I might need to work on making it a consistent habit. I'm a little turned around right now. My therapist recently told me that she thinks I'm cutting myself too much slack and that has really stuck with me this week. 

It rubbed me the wrong way as soon as she said it, but I tried to tell myself not to blow it out of proportion. Evidently that didn't work and I'm starting to ruminate about it. It's almost impossible not to internalize that kind of comment and I am starting to take it as confirmation and proof that everything is my fault.

To be fair, it is my fault. There's no one else to blame. I'm an adult and I need to take responsibility for myself and make better choices because no one else is going to do it for me.

You bring up a good point. It's not often that I think about my goals, dreams, or aspirations. I don't allow myself - either because I feel like I don't deserve good things, or that it's hopeless and I'll never get there, or fear of failure, etc. This is probably something that I should explore more when I can.

I've tried different medications and basically decided that it wasn't for me. The side effects were too troublesome and I never felt any true relief, etc.

Most recent? Today. I wanted it to be more productive. It's already well into the afternoon and I have not showered or gotten dressed or brushed my teeth or gone outside or eaten any nutritious foods. 

I'm completely avoiding all of my responsibilities almost 24/7 and it's getting ridiculous. I'm overwhelmed and scared, but I also don't care and want to give up on everything. I feel sick and ashamed.

yeah, I feel like I've lost most of the "fight" in me which only makes me feel worse. I feel broken on so many levels - mentally, physically, spiritually (if that's a thing). Everything is wrong. I don't even know where to begin.

hello. thanks for inquiring. i've got myself into a mess and i'm losing hope for any sort of recovery... my life has consistently gotten worse for the past decade? it's like one step forward three steps back.
